title: Multi-region evidence streaming & guaranteed delivery for residency/retention events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Deliver a resilient, auditable pipeline and webhook contract for emitting residency, retention-change, and evidence-ready events to downstream systems and customer endpoints across multiple regions. Provide strong delivery guarantees (exactly-once as near as practical, with deduplication and clear at-least-once semantics for edge cases), signing/encryption, delivery backpressure handling, and automated evidence bundling for audit exports.

Goals:
- Define a compact webhook contract for residency/retention/evidence events with idempotency keys, residency tags, and retention TTL metadata.
- Implement a multi-region fan-out broker that routes events to region-specific endpoints and to long-term evidence storage.
- Provide dropdown for tenants to opt into real-time webhooks vs. batched evidence bundles.
- Ensure traceability: every emitted event must include request_id, model_version, dataset_tag, and residency_zone.
- Support signed payloads (Ed25519) and per-customer public key registration.
- Build observable SLIs: delivery_success_rate, average_delivery_latency, webhook_queue_depth, dedup_rate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract doc published and approved by Security/Legal (link below).
- End-to-end demo: change retention for tenant X -> webhook emitted -> customer ack received -> evidence bundle created in S3 with residency tag.
- Delivery SLA: 99.9% successful delivery to registered endpoints in same region within 30s under normal load (burstable to 5m under load with backoff).
- Idempotency: duplicate events deduplicated by idempotency_key within 7 days.
- Evidence bundles encrypted with tenant KMS, stored with region metadata and retention TTL enforcement.

High-level design decisions / trade-offs:
- Fan-out architecture using a regional broker (Kafka-like) per region to keep residency constraints simple; global control plane records subscriptions. This keeps data plane in-region for residency-sensitive payloads.
- Delivery semantics: We target effectively-once by storing broker-offset + delivered-target checksums; full exactly-once across arbitrary third-party endpoints is infeasible, so we provide idempotency and durable retry queues for at-least-once delivery guarantee.
- Bundling cadence: default 10m batches for evidence exports to balance freshness and cost; allow customers to choose hourly/daily.
- Signing vs mutual TLS: support both; signing is default to avoid certificate ops for external partners.

Webhook contract (example):
POST /v1/compliance/events HTTP/1.1
Headers:
  Content-Type: application/json
  X-Redwood-Event: residency.change
  X-Redwood-Idempotency: rwd-evt-<uuid>
  X-Redwood-Signature: ed25519 <base64sig>
Payload (JSON):
  event_id: "rwd-evt-<uuid>",
  event_type: "residency.change",
  tenant_id: "acct_42",
  resource: "evidence_bundle",
  resource_id: "bundle_20250212_0001",
  timestamp: "2025-02-12T17:22:10Z",
  residency_zone: "eu-west-1",
  retention_ttl_days: 365,
  retention_policy_source: "admin_console:v2",
  bundle_url: "https://s3.eu-west-1.redwood-inference/internal/bundles/..",
  meta: {"model_version":"gptx-4.1", "request_id":"req-123"}

Delivery semantics and retries:
- Immediate attempt, exponential backoff with jitter up to 5 retries, then move to dead-letter queue per tenant/endpoint.
- Outbound queue persists to disk (leveldb-backed segments) to survive process restarts.
- On 2xx responses we consider delivery success; 409/422 treated idempotent/fatal; 5xx/timeout retried.
- Customers can ack receipts with X-Redwood-Ack: event_id to short-circuit retries (optional).

Retention enforcement flow:
- Console/API update sets tenant retention TTL. Control plane writes change event and triggers re-evaluation job for existing evidence records in the tenant's region.
- Re-evaluation runs as best-effort background job (bounded parallelism and rate-limited) that emits individual deletion events to region-local workers.

Observability and ops:
- Dashboards: per-tenant delivery success, average latency, retry histogram, DLQ size.
- Tracing: events carry traceparent to correlate with originating request.
- Alerting: delivery_success_rate < 99.5% for 5m -> P1 pager.

Security & compliance:
- All evidence bundles encrypted with tenant KMS (customer-managed if configured).
- Signing keys rotation policy and webhook public-key registry UI.
- Audit log of all outbound deliveries persisted for 1 year by default; exportable.

Notes on implementation scope:
Phase 1 (MVP): contract, single-region broker + outbound dispatcher, signing, retries, DLQ, console subscription UI, evidence bundling job.
Phase 2: multi-region active brokers, cross-region replication for control metadata, advanced backpressure (windowed batching), customer-managed endpoints with mTLS, SLA instrumentation.

Design artifacts and references:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMPLIANCE/pages/Multi-Region+Evidence+Streaming+Design
- Design slides (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_evidence_streaming_design
- API contract PRD: https://docs.redwood-inference.internal/compliance/events-contract-v1.md

Implementation notes:
- Broker implementation will extend the existing eventing module (platform/eventing) to support per-tenant residency_tag and per-endpoint cursors.
- Storage for bundles uses regional S3 buckets with prefixing: s3://evidence-<region>/tenant/<tenant_id>/bundles/.
- Use existing kms-integration library for envelope encryption.
updates: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off design review. Shared Confluence doc and initial API contract. Requested security review for signature schema.

2025-02-18 - Miguel Torres: POC outbound dispatcher implemented (single-region). Verified idempotency via idempotency_key stored in key-value store. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9123
2025-02-21 - Priya Menon (Security): Reviewed signing approach. Requested inclusion of public-key rotation plan and revocation endpoints. Added security checklist items.
2025-02-25 - Miguel Torres: Integrated ed25519 signing using existing key registry service. Added header verification and signature validation middleware. Demo video: https://loom.com/share/abcd1234

2025-02-27 - Nico Becker (SRE): Load-tested dispatcher under simulated spike (5000 events/s) with 5 regional brokers. Queue depth grows but backpressure kicks in at configured threshold; observed 3% increase in p50 latency. Action: add adaptive batching (follow-up).

2025-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Security review requested completion. Planning meeting scheduled 2025-03-04 with Legal to confirm retention-export disclosures. Next: add DLQ reprocessing CLI and per-tenant delivery config in Console.
